directions.label: They counted days, toward a day they meant to leave.
directions.speech: Rows like that are a calendar. Somebody had a day picked out.

gentle.good: Rows like that are a calendar. Someone had a day they were waiting for.
gentle.bad: Neat rows, kept to the end. A calendar with a day circled somewhere, and someone that careful would have reached it.

loyal.good: We'd count days too, if we were left behind to wait for our own.
loyal.bad: Rows kept for the ones who went on ahead. Any of us would count days for the others. It's days.

directions.label: They counted sleeps. There are no days down here.
directions.speech: There's no sun down here to count days by. Sleeps are the only thing that comes round.

patient.good: No sun to count by down here. You count what comes round. Sleeps.
patient.bad: Short marks, all one length. Could be sleeps, could be meals. A full row counted twice would settle it.

inquisitive.good: Short marks, all one length. That's someone waking up and doing it before anything else.
inquisitive.bad: One stroke each waking, hundreds of them. I'd want to know how thin they'd got by the last row.

practical.good: Sleeps. It's how you ration when you can't see the sky. One mark, one portion.
practical.bad: One mark a sleep, one portion a sleep. That much rationing means a store, somewhere near this wall.

directions.label: The count kept their hands busy. It wasn't for anything.
directions.speech: Look how neat they are. That's somebody giving their hands something to do.

blunt.good: Look how neat they are. That's somebody giving their hands something to do so they wouldn't think.
blunt.bad: Hundreds of neat marks and not one step toward the stair. Busy hands, idle legs, and that's what killed them.

dry-wit.good: Hundreds of them and not one crooked. You'd go mad doing that. Then again, they probably did.
dry-wit.bad: Hundreds of perfect rows. Someone had all the time in the world and spent it on a wall. Admirable, truly.

directions.label: The marks can't be trusted. The walls here shift.
directions.speech: Our chalk's a hand higher than we put it. I wouldn't read much off these walls.

cautious.good: Our chalk's a hand higher than we put it. I wouldn't trust anything written on these walls.
cautious.bad: Our chalk moved. These could have moved. For all we know this is our own count and we don't remember it.

seeks-meaning.good: The walls here don't hold still. Whatever was counted, the wall's been changing the sum.
seeks-meaning.bad: Our chalk climbed, and so did theirs. Twice is a pattern. The wall wants these read wrong.

directions.label: They stopped on their own and left.
directions.speech: The last mark doesn't skid. Whoever cut it lifted the blade off the stone.

patient.good: The last mark doesn't skid. Whoever cut it lifted the blade off the stone.
patient.bad: The end of the groove looks clean in this light. Torchlight lies, though. Hold it closer.

bold.good: Clean lift at the end. They put the blade down and went on, under their own power.
bold.bad: Clean lift, so they walked off alone with one blade. If they could manage that, we can do it faster.

inquisitive.good: No scrape at the end of the groove. The blade came away on purpose.
inquisitive.bad: A clean lift. They set the blade down and walked off to wherever they died. I'd like to find the place.

directions.label: Something made them stop.
directions.speech: You lift it the same way when you hear something behind you.

cautious.good: You lift the blade like that when you hear something behind you. I've done it.
cautious.bad: Half a stroke, with the room open behind them the whole time. Something came through that door. Who's watching ours?

blunt.good: Half a mark is somebody interrupted. They sat with their back to the room, and that was their mistake.
blunt.bad: A half stroke, back to the door. Too busy counting to look behind them. A child would have known better.

dry-wit.good: Hundreds of marks, then half of one. Either they heard something or they got bored. I don't like either.
dry-wit.bad: Something interrupted them halfway through a stroke. Rude of it. I'd rather not meet anything with manners like that.

directions.label: They lost interest in the count.
directions.speech: If it was only to keep their hands busy, they found something else to do with them.

blunt.good: If the counting was only to keep their hands busy, they found something else to do with them.
blunt.bad: Hundreds of marks, then half of one. They couldn't even finish the one thing they'd been doing.

practical.good: A count that isn't for anything is easy to drop. Something more useful came along.
practical.bad: A count that bought them nothing. The moment something worth having turned up, they dropped it. So would I.

lines.subject: The prints in the empty room

directions.label: The counter made them, walking down from the wall.
directions.speech: They got up from that wall and walked somewhere. It could have been here.

loyal.good: They got up from that wall and went after their own people. These are their steps.
loyal.bad: They'd have gone after their own people, same as any of us would. These are their steps, and I'll hear nothing else.

gentle.good: They got up from that wall and walked somewhere. It could have been here.
gentle.bad: Prints that go in and stop. They came this far looking for the others, and the others were here. That's how I'll read it.

directions.label: Someone else made them.
directions.speech: Or anyone else. Plenty came down here and didn't walk back out.

blunt.good: Prints stop in half the rooms down here. Don't hang a story on these.
blunt.bad: Prints in, none out, same as half the rooms on this floor. Another fool who didn't check behind them.

cautious.good: Could be anyone's. I'd rather not find out whose by following them.
cautious.bad: Prints in, none out. Whoever made them could still be standing somewhere we haven't looked. Backs to the wall.

practical.good: Prints going in and none out turn up on every floor. I'd not spend a candle tying these to that wall.
practical.bad: Prints in, none out, so whatever they carried is still in here. Check the corners before we go.

directions.label: The extra portion was kept for whoever came back.
directions.speech: One portion wrapped twice, apart from the rest. You keep that for someone walking back in.

loyal.good: One portion wrapped twice, apart from the rest. You keep that for whoever of yours walks back in.
loyal.bad: One portion set apart for whoever came back. You don't leave your own without that. It was for theirs, whatever anyone says.

humble.good: One set apart. They thought someone would come back hungry. I'd have forgotten to.
humble.bad: Still wrapped. Whoever it was for never came for it. I'd not have made it this far myself.

directions.label: The extra portion was for someone already gone.
directions.speech: Or for someone who wasn't coming back. Wrapped twice so it would keep a long time.

gentle.good: Or for someone who wasn't coming back. Wrapped twice so it would keep a long time.
gentle.bad: Wrapped twice, the way you lay something by a grave. You only take that much care for someone who'll be glad of it.

seeks-meaning.good: Wrapped twice and set apart. That's an offering more than a ration.
seeks-meaning.bad: Set apart for the dead, and we've broken the wrapping. That will be counted against us somewhere.

directions.label: Nothing ties the bundle to the wall.
directions.speech: A bundle and a wall a floor apart. Nothing in either one points at the other.

practical.good: A bundle and a wall a floor apart. Nothing in either one points at the other.
practical.bad: A floor between the bundle and the wall, and no name on either. Whoever it was for, it's ours now. Divide it up.

patient.good: Different floor, maybe a different year. I'd need more than a knot to tie them together.
patient.bad: A knot, a wall, and a floor between them. Not enough to tie them together, not enough to pull them apart. Leave it open.

directions.label: They never came back up.
directions.speech: Everyone we've passed down here was going one way.

blunt.good: Everyone we've passed down here was going one way.
blunt.bad: The rows end where they end, and no one has added a mark since. They're bones somewhere below us.

humble.good: I don't think they did. I don't think I would have.
humble.bad: Hundreds of sleeps, and they still went down alone. I'd have done worse. They're not coming back up.

directions.label: They found another wall and kept counting.
directions.speech: They kept that count for hundreds of sleeps. Wherever they stopped next, they'd have started another wall.

gentle.good: They kept that count for hundreds of sleeps. Wherever they stopped next, they'd have started another wall.
gentle.bad: A hand that steady doesn't stop. They found the others below and started a new wall for all of them.

bold.good: They went down on their own feet and kept going. There'll be another wall below. Let's find it.
bold.bad: Another wall further down, and they reached it alone with one blade. We'll get there faster if we stop resting.

directions.label: The counter cut it.
directions.speech: Same habit of putting things on a wall. It fits the one who kept the count.

seeks-meaning.good: Same habit of putting things on a wall. It fits the one who kept the count.
seeks-meaning.bad: The same habit of writing on walls, and the warning sits right where we'd pass. It was left for us.

humble.good: Maybe the counter, further down and more frightened. I'd carve badly too, by then.
humble.bad: Their hand, shaking by then. Mine would be worse. I can't tell one cut from another, so call it theirs.

directions.label: A different hand cut it.
directions.speech: The count was cut slow and even. This was hacked in fast. Not the same hand on the blade.

craft-pride.good: The count was cut slow and even. This was hacked in fast. Not the same hand on the blade.
craft-pride.bad: Look at that work. Whoever kept the count would never cut something this ugly.

inquisitive.good: These strokes are deep and uneven. The count's are shallow and all alike. Two people.
inquisitive.bad: Deep, uneven strokes cut in a hurry. Someone had minutes left. I'd want to know how many.

directions.label: Two kinds of people cut it, and they don't agree.
directions.speech: The closed ones are cut tight, the open ones wide. Somebody meant each of them.

inquisitive.good: The closed ones are cut tight, the open ones wide. Somebody meant each of them, and not the same somebody.
inquisitive.bad: Two kinds of cutter, and the closed ones always sit by a body. I'd want to see how the dead were set there.

seeks-meaning.good: Closed and open. Two readings of one mark, and the people cutting them never agreed.
seeks-meaning.bad: Closed on one wall, open on the next, all the way down. They're arguing about us, and we'll have to take a side.

directions.label: One cutter, careless which way it turns.
directions.speech: Same depth of groove on both. One tool made them. Which way it turns could be how the stone sat.

craft-pride.good: Same depth of groove on both. One tool made them. Which way it turns could be how the stone sat.
craft-pride.bad: Sloppy work, both kinds. One hack with a chisel and no plan.

dry-wit.good: Or one person who never could remember which way they'd done it last time.
dry-wit.bad: Same groove depth on both. One cutter with a terrible memory. Lovely work otherwise.

directions.label: It's one mark, seen from different sides.
directions.speech: The merchant's goods carry it whichever way the cloth lies. Turn one over and it opens.

practical.good: The merchant's goods carry it whichever way the cloth lies. Turn one over and it opens.
practical.bad: The merchant sells it both ways round. So it means whatever pays.

patient.good: Three of the merchant's pieces closed, two open, every one the same burn. Depends how the cloth was folded.
patient.bad: Open or closed depending on the fold, and I've only looked at one cloth. Three more before we write it.

directions.label: Closed. It means keep this shut.
directions.speech: Every closed one we've passed had something behind it with claws.

cautious.good: Every closed one we've passed had something behind it with claws.
cautious.bad: Closed means keep out. Every one we passed had claws behind it, and I'd wager the open ones do too.

blunt.good: The closed ones had guards. Whoever cut them wanted people kept out. People like us.
blunt.bad: Every closed one had a guard behind it, and every guard is dead now. Whoever cut the mark should have cut it deeper.

directions.label: Open. It means come in.
directions.speech: The open ones have cups set in them. You don't set a cup for someone you want out.

gentle.good: The open ones have cups set in them. You don't set a cup for someone you want out.
gentle.bad: Cups set in the open ones, like places at a table. Someone was expecting company, and they'd have been glad of us.

bold.good: The open ones had cups and altars. Somebody wanted visitors, and kept a place for them.
bold.bad: Cups in the open ones, so somebody wanted visitors. We'll take the invitation all the way to the bottom.

fragments.text: Tally marks scratched into the wall, hundreds, one hand, neat rows. The last mark stops halfway.
Every mark in a row is the same length. No longer mark anywhere to close off a week.

remark.text: Every mark's the same length. Counting days, you'd cut a longer one every seventh.

patient.good: Every mark's the same length. Counting days, you'd cut a longer one every seventh.
patient.bad: Every mark the same length, in this row at least. Count another row before anyone changes the page.

inquisitive.good: No week marks anywhere. Someone keeping days would have cut every seventh one longer without thinking.
inquisitive.bad: Same length, every one, for hundreds of sleeps. By the end they weren't counting anything. Just cutting.

fragments.text: Footprints lead into an empty room. None lead out.
A bundle tied at the foot of a wall. The rations inside are wrapped in portions. One is set apart, wrapped twice.
Chalk marks left on the way down sit a hand's width higher than they were made.
A warning cut into the wall in a hurry and left unfinished. The strokes are deep and uneven.
A spiral scratched beside a guarded hoard, coiled tight and closed like a knot.
A spiral carved into an altar, unwound and open at its center.
The same spiral burned into every piece of the merchant's goods, turned whichever way the cloth was laid.

echoes.text: Below the last mark, two heel scuffs in the grit, both pointing toward the way down.
The rows end where they ended on the wall above. Nothing has been added.
Lower down, apart from the rows, one mark that looks newer than the rest.
Under the knot, a row of short marks pressed into the wax, all the same length.
The half of the spiral left on the lock was stamped. The scratches across it were cut by hand, later.
By the stair, someone has started a row of short marks, one each time they wake.
The last mark cut here is closed, the way yours always were.
The last mark cut here is open, the way yours always were.
